steps: Title globe and dossier, picked Saudi Arabia in Bab al-Mandab Burning
Executed month 1 and read the four-page debrief and the newspaper
scenarios.notes: Verdict: real art direction (illustrated scenes, serif display type, coherent palette), not a plain dashboard, but the desk still leans on text cards and the copy has generated-prose tells.

steps: Opened Yemen from the map, queued Ceasefire
Checked the desk: the order appeared there as 'Propose ceasefire to Yemen' with a 4% chance
scenarios.notes: The same order lands in the same queue from both surfaces. But map gives no confirmation, and the map menu has no success chance, which the desk shows. Played 2 months only, stopped after the second desk screen.

friction.where: Map mode, Yemen menu, first Ceasefire press
friction.happened: First press by label did nothing visible (orders stayed 1/6); second press queued it. Menu then closes silently with no toast, sound or animation, only the counter changes.
Greyed with no visible reason; the reason ('Needs 2, you have 1') exists only in a native tooltip.
Image is a 443px block with dead space to its right, and the layout jumps up about 60px when the tutorial banner is dismissed or a card is chosen. Lower half of the centre column is empty.

friction.expected: Filled pips mean what is left
friction.happened: At 0 left the three pips are filled orange while the header diamonds are all empty; the two indicators invert each other.
'CAPITAL' in header, 'Capital' in rail, diamond '1 left' on map, 'Leadership score' in mission box vs 'Score' in header, 'Orders' vs 'In person' vs 'meetings'.

friction.expected: Illustration and status match the outcome
friction.happened: Card is checkmarked green with a handshake summit scene and 'ends the call on warmer terms', while its own line says 'Propose ceasefire to Yemen (failed)' in red.
Approval shows 64 to 58 (-6) in the crisis card but 55.0% (-9.0) in the tiles; the chronicle repeats -9.0; Score 0.0 shown as the month change.
Pins sit on top of country names (United Kingdom, Lebanon, Afghanistan, Turkey) and the mission box wraps 'now 100' awkwardly.

friction.expected: Map screenshot and next navigation respond
friction.happened: The page froze twice (screenshot timeouts of 30 s) after switching to Map mode the first time and after tapping a debrief tab; the first time it needed a driver restart. Machine load was very high, so this may be the environment, not the game.

bugs.title: Newspaper lede is garbled and headline reads like a template
steps: Execute month 1 with Back channel via Muscat
bugs.actual: Headline 'Salman on After the Riyadh airport strike: Back channel via Muscat'; lede 'On after the Riyadh airport strike, ...' with drop cap 'O' then 'n after'.

bugs.title: Newspaper hero art contradicts the decision
bugs.expected: Art matches a diplomatic back channel
bugs.actual: Full-width fighter jets and a TGT LOCK reticle, as for an air strike.

bugs.title: War card typo: 'The front moves l in your favour'
bugs.actual: A lowercase l stands where a number belongs.

bugs.title: Reform program card in the debrief shows no result on page 1
bugs.actual: Card is just the title 'Order / Reform program', with the facts only on page 3.

suggestions.what: Make every disabled map or desk button show its reason as visible text (Into the Breach shows the why on the tile)
Confirm queued orders with motion and a sound plus a stamp in the queue, the way Balatro makes each press feel physical
Give the crisis hero the full column width and a fixed layout, and fill the empty lower half of the desk with the expected outcome of the selected option
Pick one word for the resource and use it in header, rail, map and mission box; show success chance on the map menu as on the desk
Hand-edit generated prose templates (headline, lede, war line) and tie the art and the status icon to the outcome (failed order must not wear a green check and a handshake)

delight: Title screen: serif display type, globe menu with pins, and the 'Put it out, or don't.' line look authored (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/sam-desktop/001-title.png)
The globe map with a relations layer, flagged pins and dotted lines is the most game-like screen (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/sam-desktop/002-map.png)
Debrief with illustrated summit and map scenes and quoted reactions from the other leader (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/sam-desktop/012-d3b.png)
The newspaper page, as an object (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/sam-desktop/014-d5.png)

fun.reason: The month loop with named people reacting is engaging, but I only played one real month and the staff pre-fill meant I made one choice.

clarity.reason: Banner explains left, middle and right, but the vocabulary drifts and some failures have no visible reason.

visual.reason: Real art direction in title, map, scenes and paper; held back by the dead desk space, label collisions and art that contradicts outcomes.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Scenes and reactions help, yet pressing a button gives no motion or sound and the desk reads as a form.

agency.reason: Staff pre-picks everything; disabled actions hide their reason; the first map press seemed to do nothing.

realism.reason: Plausible leaders and quotes; the stats-driven prose breaks the spell.

replay.reason: Not enough seen to say; one sample of generated copy was enough to show the seams.

recommend.reason: I would show the title and map to a friend as a good-looking one; I would not claim it is hand-crafted until the copy and the feedback are fixed.

verbatim: It is better looking than I expected and I stopped assuming slop at the map, but then the newspaper opened with 'On after the Riyadh airport strike' over a bombing picture for a back channel, and the spell cracked.
